propositions: MCP transition_ticket and claim_ticket signatures omit parameters (force, reason, caused_by, ref) already supported by the library and CLI, making those write controls unreachable over MCP.
FastMCP derives JSON schemas and input models from handwritten callable signatures in _mcp_writes.py, so undeclared parameters are dropped before the adapter executes.

The handwritten MCP adapter forwarding layer independently forwards only close_class for transition and assignee for claim, so schema additions alone would not restore the missing parameters to the library core.

Runtime probes confirmed all four discriminating mechanisms: live schemas omitted the fields, real tool captures received only current kwargs, an equivalent FastMCP tool with declared fields received exact sentinels, and MCP ref selected HEAD instead of the requested commit while caused_by closed without an edge.

The 2026-08-18 operator ruling rescinds the earlier CLI/library-only force policy and establishes total parity across all surfaces (CLI, library, MCP) with absent certification as the sole audit signal.
The repair adds declared parameters to both signatures and forwards them unchanged to the existing library core, ensuring parity while preserving all existing validation and gating semantics.
